# Pin the icon, icon-link and LinkedIn grid columns

## Welcome 👋

Neo's grid can put a clickable icon in a cell: an icon, an icon with a link, or a LinkedIn profile link built from a bare handle. Each of these columns decides what the cell shows in one method, `applyRecordConfigs(config, record)`. They have small, testable rules (formatters, URL building, hiding empty cells) and no tests.

This is a **good first issue** for Hacktoberfest 2026. It needs Node.js and a clone of this repository: no Docker, no AI setup.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Reserved for first-time Neo.mjs contributors.** The maintainer team will not claim, edit, or implement this issue through **2026-10-31**. Comment here to claim it, and ask anything on this issue.

**Set up once:** follow [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone), including `npm run bundle-browser-deps`: without it the unit suite selects zero tests.

## Where things live

- Sources: `src/grid/column/Icon.mjs`, `IconLink.mjs`, `LinkedIn.mjs`
- New test file: `test/playwright/unit/grid/column/IconColumns.spec.mjs`
- Pattern to copy: `test/playwright/unit/grid/column/Component.spec.mjs` (creating a column with `Neo.create()` and a `dataField`). A plain object works as the record for these methods.

## What to cover

| Column | Case | `applyRecordConfigs(config, record)` returns |
|---|---|---|
| `Icon` | no `cellIconCls` on the column | `cellIconCls` is the record value; `hidden` is `true` when that value is falsy |
| `Icon` | a fixed `cellIconCls` on the column | that `cellIconCls`; still `hidden` when the record value is falsy |
| `IconLink` | no formatters | `url` is the record value; `label` is `record[labelField]`, or `null` without a `labelField`; `cellIconCls` comes from the column |
| `IconLink` | `urlFormatter` | `url` is `urlFormatter(value, record)` |
| `IconLink` | `labelFormatter` | `label` is `labelFormatter(x, record)`, where `x` is the `labelField` value if one is set, else the record value |
| `LinkedIn` | a bare handle, e.g. `'jane-doe'` | `url` is `'https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe/'` |
| `LinkedIn` | a value starting with `http` | kept as it is |
| `LinkedIn` | defaults | `cellIconCls` is `'fa-brands fa-linkedin'` |
| all three | a key passed in `config` | wins over the derived one (it is spread last) |

## Done when

- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/grid/column/IconColumns.spec.mjs` exists, following the pattern file's setup.
- [ ] One `test(...)` per table row.
- [ ] Test-only: if a column disagrees with a row, say so on this issue before changing `src/`.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/grid/column/IconColumns.spec.mjs` passes.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` passes.

## Out of scope

The icon components themselves, and click handling in a real grid.

## While you wait for review

You just pinned one small piece of a multi-threaded application engine: in Neo.mjs your app's code runs inside a web worker, and the main thread only paints. Two things worth ten minutes:

- **See the part nobody expects.** Run `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` and `npm run server-start`, open `apps/workstation/`, and drag a tab out of the browser window. It becomes its own OS window, still running, with the same component instances and the same worker. [Benefits: Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md) explains why that is possible.
- **Your coding agent can go much further here.** The skills this repository's AI maintainers work with are published on npm as [`neo-agent-skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/neo-agent-skills), and they need no Knowledge Base and no Memory Core. With Claude or GPT beside you, the `help wanted` issues are within reach after this one.
